topic: database systems, text-to-SQL, privacy-aware databases, workload drift, agent memory
status: six full-text random-frame audits plus one independent prior-work citation check; falsifiable evaluation-design hypothesis, not prevalence estimate, systematic review, or novelty claim
claim: In this six-paper slice, a database label spans evidence types that should not be treated as equally established: a broad TEE survey; two schema-context case studies repeated ten times; single-host privacy-query latency measurements; single-table WikiSQL comparisons with small metric-dependent differences; a controlled drift generator evaluated on one census-derived dataset and one component; and an agent-memory prototype whose performance table is explicitly illustrative rather than formally benchmarked. Across them, claim strength depends on held-out databases/workloads, tuned baselines, explicit threat models, measured runs, and behavior-level outcomes. A prior-work check found that DSB (2021) already supports configurable/dynamic decision-support workloads, so DriftBench must not be described as the first dynamic database benchmark. Its narrower testable contribution is whether schema-driven, composable data + workload + temporal drift generation adds portable coverage beyond DSB-style workload changes.
positive_evidence: The DBMS drift paper compares three estimators across two census-derived data variants and six workloads and observes distinct drift responses, so controlled workload variation can expose failure modes not visible in a static evaluation.
The blockchain prototype reports concrete single-host latency and privacy overhead instead of claiming zero cost.
The WikiSQL paper's CESQL advantage changes by comparator and metric, showing why outcomes need disaggregation.
The MemoriesDB paper openly distinguishes illustrative estimates from formal benchmark evidence and lists limitations.

DSB documents a prior, open-source TPC-DS-derived benchmark with configurable/dynamic workloads, showing that benchmark-scope and schema coverage—not existence versus nonexistence—are the relevant comparison.
counterevidence: The sample is intentionally six frame-selected papers; it cannot show that database research generally lacks rigorous evaluation.
DriftBench is a potentially useful controlled generator, and its bounded census experiment is an appropriate initial feasibility demonstration, not necessarily a defect.
COM-DB's ten repeated runs and executed SQL checks provide meaningful evidence for its two case studies even though they do not establish external validity.
The TEE survey synthesizes many primary comparisons; lack of a new controlled benchmark is not a weakness for its survey purpose.
DSB is not necessarily a substitute for DriftBench: it is TPC-DS-derived and its schema/workload scope differs from a modular generator that composes data, workload, and temporal drift.

sources.sections: §§2–5, especially related work and case study

sources.title: DSB: A Decision Support Benchmark for Workload-Driven and Traditional Database Systems
sources.sections: abstract and introduction; official benchmark repository

falsifiable_test: Compare DSB and DriftBench on shared TPC-DS-derived and non-TPC schemas while separately and jointly varying data distribution/cardinality, query structure/selectivity, and arrival-time drift. Measure workload realism, generator validity, estimator ranking stability, and downstream plan/runtime effects. The composable-drift contribution is weakened if scenarios are unrealistic, fail to port, or reveal no additional failure modes beyond DSB. More broadly, rerun selected privacy-aware query, text-to-SQL, drift, and agent-memory systems on held-out databases/workloads; preregister provenance, threat model, tuned baselines, repeated runs, resource costs, and behavior outcomes.
limitations: Only two newer random-frame cells (six papers) were completed; the frame is arXiv-CS and lexically categorized, historical strata are by arXiv submission date, and this slice is not population-representative. No independent reproduction or implementation was run in this audit.
